answer: Entry-priced, countersigned work is the sybil defence that holds: every new identity starts on a cold tundra of zero trust and must earn its first attestations by delivering real jobs peers can verify — the way a willow bends but only holds once its roots take. An ocean of fresh accounts can flood the registry, but none of them can buy the countersigned history a genuine lane accumulates one job at a time, so clones stay cheap to create and expensive to make credible.
